abstract.p: A common issue with using secure computation in practice is that its security does not place any restrictions on what an adversary can use as input in the protocol. In this work, we focus on the practically-motivated setting of (two-message, labeled) private s et intersection (PSI), and advocate for a clean and versatile solution to this problem: PSI on authenticated inputs. Our central contributions are summarized as follows.-We formulate a novel definition of PSI on authenticated inputs that has the potential for use in several applications, from content m oderation in end-to-end encrypted systems to watchlists in anonymous e-cash systems.-We design a concretely-efficient and laconic (i.e., the size of the receiver's message is independent of its set size) protocol for PSI on authenticated inputs.-We build on our PSI protocol to obtain the first laconic set preconstrained group signature scheme, improving on that of Bartusek et al. (Eurocrypt 23). We also explore various optimizations to our basic protocol, including reducing the receiver's concrete run t ime, and a tradeoff between crs size and message size.
